package_info.package_manager: custom/unknown (deployed as web server code, not via public package manager)

package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is designed to facilitate adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing attacks, enabling credential and session token theft, bypassing multi-factor authentication (MFA), and evading detection through advanced cloaking, browser fingerprinting, and abuse of legitimate code hosting services. Its core functionality is malicious by design, targeting user authentication flows to compromise accounts.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when victim visits phishing site and interacts with login form)
execution_context.file_location: server.js / index.php / main web server file (deployed on phishing domains)
required_permissions: network (to proxy requests and communicate with external services)
filesystem (for logging or exfiltration of captured data)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code acts as a reverse proxy when the victim visits the phishing site and submits login data, forwarding requests to login.microsoftonline.com, intercepting credentials and session cookies from the victim, and logging or exfiltrating this data, resulting in credential and session token theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and logging credentials and session cookies during proxying of authentication requests is a direct indicator of adversary-in-the-middle phishing activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate login page or proxy should never capture or log user credentials or session cookies; such data should only be handled by the intended authentication service.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Reverse proxies are used for load balancing or security in legitimate infrastructure, but never to intercept or log authentication data.
key_indicators: Capturing and logging credentials and session cookies from authentication flows
Forwarding traffic to legitimate service to avoid user suspicion
Presence of code that conditionally logs sensitive data based on request URL

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when victim submits credentials via phishing form)
required_permissions: network (to exfiltrate credentials to attacker infrastructure)
filesystem (to store credentials locally for later retrieval)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the victim submits credentials, the code extracts the credentials from the request body, sends them via POST to an attacker-controlled C2 server, and optionally writes them to a local file for later retrieval, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating user credentials to an external, attacker-controlled server is a clear sign of malicious intent and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate authentication handlers should never transmit user credentials to untrusted third-party domains or store them in unprotected local files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for exfiltrating authentication credentials to external infrastructure.
key_indicators: Outbound POST requests containing credentials to non-corporate or attacker-controlled domains
Local logging of sensitive credentials in files such as creds.log
Parsing and handling of authentication data outside of legitimate authentication flows

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when session cookies are set by Microsoft login during proxying)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when session cookies are set by the legitimate Microsoft login during proxying, the code captures these cookies, sends them via POST to an attacker-controlled server, and optionally writes them to a local file, enabling session hijacking and MFA bypass.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Capturing and exfiltrating session cookies allows attackers to hijack authenticated sessions and bypass multi-factor authentication, which is a direct method for account takeover.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Session cookies should remain confidential between the client and the legitimate authentication server; they should never be transmitted to third parties or stored insecurely.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for exfiltrating authentication or session cookies to external infrastructure.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of authentication/session cookies to attacker-controlled endpoints
Local storage of session cookies in files such as cookies.log
Network requests containing session data outside of normal authentication flows

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when phishing page is loaded in victim's browser)
execution_context.file_location: client-side javascript in phishing HTML page
required_permissions: browser fingerprinting APIs (to detect automated analysis or security scanners)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the phishing page is loaded, the code fingerprints the browser to detect automated analysis or security scanners, and conditionally cloaks the phishing content by redirecting to a benign site or displaying the phishing form only to real users, thereby evading detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Cloaking and browser fingerprinting are advanced evasion techniques used to avoid detection by automated security tools and researchers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate login pages do not alter content or behavior based on browser fingerprinting or the presence of analysis tools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate sites use basic fingerprinting for anti-fraud, but not to selectively hide malicious content or evade security analysis.
key_indicators: Detection of headless browsers or known security scanner user-agents
Conditional display or redirection based on browser fingerprinting results
Client-side logic to evade automated analysis by showing benign content

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when victim clicks phishing link in email or opens HTML attachment)
execution_context.file_location: redirector script (embedded in HTML attachment or initial phishing domain)
required_permissions: network (to perform redirection to phishing infrastructure)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the victim clicks the phishing link or opens the HTML attachment, the code immediately redirects the browser to the main phishing proxy site, chaining the victim through multiple domains to evade email security scanners and automated analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chained redirects through multiple unrelated domains are a common tactic to evade automated URL analysis and security solutions, making it harder to detect the final phishing destination.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate email links should not redirect users through unrelated or suspicious domains, especially not to obfuscate the true destination.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some marketing emails use redirects for tracking, but not to conceal phishing infrastructure or evade security controls.
key_indicators: Chained redirects to unrelated or newly registered domains
Use of obfuscated or non-corporate domains in redirection chains
Presence of inline scripts that perform immediate redirection to phishing infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email containing a malicious link or HTML attachment that initiates redirection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is redirected to the phishing proxy site.

attack_chain.action: Victim is redirected through one or more intermediary domains to the main phishing proxy, obfuscating the final destination.
attack_chain.leads_to: Phishing proxy page is loaded in victim's browser.

attack_chain.action: Phishing proxy page loads in the victim's browser and performs browser fingerprinting and cloaking to evade automated analysis.
attack_chain.leads_to: If not detected as automated analysis, the phishing login form is shown to the victim.

attack_chain.action: Victim enters credentials into the phishing form, which are proxied to the real Microsoft login page by the malicious server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credentials and session cookies are intercepted by the malicious proxy.

attack_chain.action: Intercepted credentials and session cookies are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure and optionally stored locally.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's account, potentially bypassing MFA.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen credentials and session tokens to log in, access emails, and perform further malicious actions such as internal phishing or lateral movement.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full account compromise and potential spread within the organization.

behavioral_signatures: Reverse proxying of authentication pages (e.g., login.microsoftonline.com) with interception and logging of credentials or session cookies
Credential and session cookie exfiltration via outbound POST requests to attacker-controlled domains
Client-side browser fingerprinting and cloaking logic to evade automated analysis or security scanners
Chained URL redirects through multiple unrelated or newly registered domains prior to landing on phishing infrastructure
file_indicators: Presence of server-side proxy scripts forwarding requests to login.microsoftonline.com
Local files logging credentials or cookies (e.g., creds.log, cookies.log) on web server
Client-side scripts in HTML pages that check for headless browsers or known security scanner user-agents
Inline JavaScript in email attachments or landing pages that perform immediate redirection
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests containing credentials or session cookies to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., /collect, /cookies endpoints)
Phishing domains mimicking Microsoft or financial services, especially those not associated with legitimate organizations
Use of legitimate code hosting services (e.g., codesandbox.io, glitch.me) as part of phishing infrastructure or redirection chains
Multiple HTTP redirects in sequence, especially involving non-corporate or suspicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web servers acting as reverse proxies to login.microsoftonline.com that also capture or log credentials and session cookies. Detect outbound POST requests from web servers or client browsers containing authentication data to non-corporate or suspicious domains. Flag client-side scripts that perform browser fingerprinting or conditionally display content based on analysis detection. Identify chained redirects in email links or attachments, especially those passing through newly registered or unrelated domains. Correlate these behaviors with known phishing IOCs and abuse of code hosting platforms to identify AiTM phishing campaigns.
